bottleneck.description: Small Ku-band GEO SATCOM-as-a-service operator (one owned satellite Ovzon 3, plus leased Intelsat capacity) with proprietary mobile terminals serving defense/NATO customers in a crowded competitive field.

dependency.key_customers: U.S. Department of Defense (historic anchor), Swedish FMV (1.04B SEK 2025 order), European NATO customer (240 MSEK Q4 2025), public-safety, NGO, and maritime.
dependency.key_suppliers: Intelsat (leased transponder capacity), Maxar/SSL (Ovzon 3 satellite bus), launch providers (SpaceX launched Ovzon 3), terminal contract manufacturers.

editorial.notes: Ovzon competes head-on with Viasat-Inmarsat, SES, Iridium, and increasingly SpaceX/Starshield PLEO services in the DoD/NATO SATCOM-as-a-Service market — DoD's PLEO program alone expanded from $900M to $13B ceiling, signaling abundant alternatives. Their differentiation is the small high-throughput on-the-move terminal portfolio (T6/T7/P20/P30) which gives some product moat, but Ku-band GEO capacity is a commodity and customers have many viable substitutes. Not a structural choke-point; financial position has improved sharply in 2025 (revenue 735 MSEK, EBITDA +291 MSEK, 1B+ SEK backlog), so no going-concern flag warranted.
